sequences.title: I'm watching people or exits
sequences.subtitle: Your eyes keep sweeping the room for something not quite right.

steps.text: Look around once, slowly.
steps.hint: You are not searching for danger. You are only learning where you are.

steps.text: Name three neutral objects in front of you.
steps.hint: A colour, a shape, a piece of furniture. Ordinary things with no special meaning.

steps.text: Notice both feet on the floor, and press them down gently.
steps.hint: The ground is holding you right now.

steps.text: Release your tongue, then your jaw, then your shoulders.
steps.hint: In that order. Do not force any muscle.

steps.text: Pick one ordinary thing in front of you and rest your attention on it.
steps.hint: A book, a cup, a screen. Anything that needs no watching.

sequences.title: A sound or movement startled me
sequences.subtitle: Your body jumped before your mind knew what happened.

steps.text: Name the sound you heard.
steps.hint: A door, a car, something dropped. Even if unsure, name the closest guess.

steps.text: Say to yourself: I am in ... and today is ...
steps.hint: Out loud if you can.

steps.text: Notice three signs that you are in the present, not in a memory.
steps.hint: The light, the sounds, your clothes, the device in your hand.

steps.text: Five breaths, with the out-breath slightly longer than the in-breath.
steps.hint: Light breaths. Do not hold, and do not force your chest full.

substitute.text: Press your palms together five times, slowly.
substitute.hint: A gentle squeeze, then a longer release.

steps.text: Return to a small part of what you were doing before the sound.
steps.hint: One part. Not all of it.

sequences.title: My body feels activated
sequences.subtitle: Your heart, your chest, or tension through the muscles.

steps.text: Feet on the floor, and press down.
steps.hint: Notice the pressure. Do not analyse it.

steps.text: Drop your shoulders away from your ears, and release your jaw.
steps.hint: Skip any area that hurts.

steps.text: Move slowly: stand, take a few steps, or stretch your arms.
steps.hint: Movement discharges activation faster than stillness.

steps.text: Calm breaths, with the out-breath longer than the in-breath.
steps.hint: If you feel lightheaded, return to normal breathing immediately.

substitute.text: Keep moving gently for another half minute.

steps.text: Choose one small thing to return to now.
steps.hint: Activation often settles while you are doing something, not before.

sequences.title: I feel detached, or things seem unreal
sequences.subtitle: As if watching yourself from a distance, or the room looks strange.

steps.text: Keep your eyes open and lift your head a little.
steps.hint: Do not close your eyes in this state in particular.

steps.text: Say out loud: the place, the date, and roughly the time.
steps.hint: The sound of your own voice is part of the grounding.

steps.text: Press your feet into the floor with moderate force, then release.
steps.hint: Repeat two or three times.

steps.text: Hold something with a clear texture and describe how it feels.
steps.hint: A key, fabric, a cold cup. Putting it into words matters.

steps.text: Make one short, slow movement: stand, or take two steps.
steps.hint: Movement outward, not meditation inward.

sequences.title: My thoughts are predicting danger
sequences.subtitle: Your mind is building a scenario of what might happen.

steps.text: Say: I notice my mind is predicting that ...
steps.hint: Notice the thought. Do not argue with it.

steps.text: What evidence exists right now? And what suggests this is a false alarm?
steps.hint: Both together. You are not in a courtroom.

steps.text: Ask: is there something to act on now, or do I need to let the wave pass?
steps.hint: A prediction is not evidence by itself.

steps.text: Feet on the floor, jaw released.
steps.hint: Return to the body before deciding.

steps.text: Choose one small action to return to.
steps.hint: Even if the thought is still there.

sequences.title: I cannot settle down to sleep
sequences.subtitle: Your body is tired but the alarm is still running.

steps.text: Lower the light and move the screen away from your face.
steps.hint: You do not need complete darkness.

steps.text: Decide not to look at the clock until morning.
steps.hint: Counting the hours left to sleep raises activation.

steps.text: Tense each muscle group for four seconds, then release for longer: face, shoulders, hands, legs.
steps.hint: Skip any painful area.

steps.text: A calm out-breath, slightly longer, with no holding.
steps.hint: If focusing on the breath bothers you, the next step is enough on its own.

substitute.text: Notice the weight of your body on the bed, point by point.

steps.text: Allow yourself to rest even if sleep has not come yet.
steps.hint: Rest has value on its own. Sleep arrives more easily once we stop chasing it.

sequences.title: I don't know, I just feel on edge
sequences.subtitle: You do not have to name the feeling in order to work with it.

steps.text: Look around once, slowly.
steps.hint: Once is enough.

steps.text: Say to yourself: I am in ... and today is ...
steps.hint: The place and the date.

steps.text: Feet on the floor, shoulders down, jaw released.
steps.hint: Three points, in order.

steps.text: Name three things you can see and two you can hear.
steps.hint: Anything that is actually there.

steps.text: Choose one small step to return to now.
steps.hint: The goal is not for the feeling to disappear.
